thesis_text:
Bottom line: for D. E. Shaw & Co. (Quant/SWE, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Stated bar is raw analytical ability over credentials: the firm says it weighs talent, curiosity and analytical thinking more than any particular skill or experience, and requires no finance background. Treat that as the stated screen only - no public data in this record can confirm the revealed screen, and community sources consistently describe the technical interviews as very demanding (labeled anecdotal in interview_styles).

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.

We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).
